decisions: CSharp WasmBrowserLlvmRuntimePlatform189-206 treats browser_write return as a nonzero success flag, validates unsigned length against Int32.MaxValue before host call, and publishes requested byte length only on success; failure publishes zero. Existing browser production host and exact-output verifier both return1 for success, including zero-byte writes.

SLG emitWasmTextRuntime574-591 incorrectly compares the status to byte length, causing false failure on zero-byte and multi-byte writes. Reuse the canonical CSharp sollang_write primitive contract and let print test its status independently for data and newline, keeping sticky failure state.

CSharp real WASM status1,2,-1 and0 cases pass before SLG edit, using empty UTF8 writes and multi-byte output. Normal target controls remain unchanged; do not weaken expected exit or change the host to byte-count semantics.

The prior parallel compiler now passes all Windows7 and compiles Wasm649 with defined%v12. This distinct runtime ABI mismatch justifies a new bounded source build; retain both old products and failed records.
